subject: Runway sequestration request for HaloAI (late-stage)
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Jul 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Runway sequestration request for HaloAI (late-stage)

Team — quick ask on a late-stage opportunity that just committed verbally. HaloAI (Samir Khan) is asking for a short-term capacity guarantee while they finalize procurement (DocuSign in flight). High level: they plan to go live with a quantized 70B model on our Dedicated offering and want a 30–45 day runway where we soft-sequester capacity so they don’t get pre-empted while contracts close.

Key ask: provision a provisional soft sequestration of 12 GPUs in WEST-1 (preferentially from Dedicated pool v2) starting as soon as ops confirms — this is a soft hold (not billing yet) but must be exclusive to the deal for the window. They will sign a small MOU / pay a nominal commitment once legal approves.

Why now: deal goes to final approval on the 16th, procurement expects signatures by the 19th, but they want to mitigate risk of model performance being impacted by pre-emption during the first 2 weeks of prod. If we don’t reserve, they may push to a competitor with guaranteed runway.

I attached the draft MOU and Halo’s capacity profile (halo_capacity_profile.csv). They included a traffic forecast and model footprint — see their email I’m forwarding in a follow-up message.

Can Ops/Capacity jump on a quick pre-check: availability, number of racks needed, and whether we can tag these GPUs for HaloAI and mark them as soft-sequestered through the console (no autoscaling on those nodes)? Also need recommendations on tagging + routing policy (early fallback to a smaller quantized variant).

If doable, please respond with a play-by-play and ETA; I need to update Sales leadership and the customer this afternoon.

Thanks —
Michael Grant
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mobile: +1 (415) 555-0134

Attachments: halo_deal_mou.pdf (stub), halo_capacity_profile.csv (stub)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Jul 2029 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Runway sequestration request for HaloAI (late-stage)

Michael — thanks for the heads-up. A couple quick clarifying Qs so Capacity can scope the reservation properly: 

1) Can you confirm the expected replica sizing (GPUs/replica) and the desired number of replicas for the initial go-live vs. 30-day ramp? The CSV helps but I want explicit targets for allocation.
2) Expected steady-state and peak concurrency (rps/qps) and average tokens per request — we use that to estimate sustained throughput and whether batching will help.
3) Is this a hard exclusivity requirement (no other tenants on those GPUs) or is the customer OK with soft isolation (affinity + eviction priority)?
4) Any SLAs being requested that would change placement (e.g., <100ms p50 for 2048 tokens)?

Operational notes: we can tag capacity and mark a soft hold in the console for up to 60 days. Hard reservations require a committed Dedicated contract (billing) and Legal signoff. For a 12-GPU soft hold we need sign-off from Capacity lead and we’ll create an internal ticket to lock tags and routing flags.

If you can paste Halo’s forecast (or ask Samir to send a short traffic summary) I’ll run the quick-fit analysis and confirm if WEST-1 has 12 contiguous GPUs that can be isolated without impacting current commitments. ETA: if we get the numbers today, I can return an availability/impact note by EOD.

-Laura
Laura Bennett
Capacity Planning Lead | Redwood Inference

From: Samir Khan <samir@haloai.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.ai>, procurement@haloai.com
Date: Wed, 3 Jul 2029 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: HaloAI production forecast & footprint (for Redwood)

Michael — thanks for looping us in. Quick summary from procurement/engineering so you can pass to Capacity: 

- Model: Halo-70B-quant (8-bit asymmetric quant)
- Replica footprint: ~4 GPUs per replica (A100 80GB equivalence) for target latency profile; benching shows we can run with 3 GPUs but prefer 4 for headroom.
- Go-live plan (initial): 3 replicas (target steady footprint = 12 GPUs)
- 30-day ramp: target 6 replicas (24 GPUs) if initial metrics look good and procurement completes.
- Traffic: anticipated steady-state 80–120 requests/sec (avg), burstable to 400 rps for short windows. Average request size ~300 tokens.
- Expected batching: yes, they will use batching with client SDK; effective tokens/sec improves by ~1.6x when batched.
- SLA ask: p90 latency target ~350–450ms for 512-token requests; flexible on p99 in early days.

Procurement: we’re moving DocuSign (MOU) today; looking to finalize the commercial by the 19th. In the interim we need the soft runway lock so we can run load testing without interruption.

Let me know if you need a quick call with our infra lead (Elena) and procurement.

Cheers,
Samir Khan
Head of Platform Engineering | HaloAI

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops_capacity@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 4 Jul 2029 14:26:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Runway sequestration request for HaloAI (late-stage)

Thanks for the details and the forwarded note from Samir — that forecast is helpful. Summary of my read and next steps: 

- Quick-fit assessment: WEST-1 can support an immediate soft-sequestration of 12 GPUs for a 30-day window without impacting active Dedicated customers. We will tag as "soft-hold:HLW-2029-07-17" and set eviction priority to low.
- Contiguity: ops can allocate across two racks (6 + 6) — not fully contiguous but we will reserve network bandwidth and priority scheduling to emulate contiguous performance.
- Oversubscribe guardrails: because Halo expects bursty peaks to 400 rps, we recommend staging with 3 replicas (12 GPUs) and enabling automatic pre-warm policy for bursts; ops to enable prefix KV cache warmup.
- Fallbacks: implement routing rule to fall back to 35B quant variant (2 GPUs/replica) if queue latency crosses 1.5s for >60s. Configure automatic model swap and notify SRE.

Action items assigned: 
- @Laura: create the internal capacity ticket and set soft-hold flag; include tag + expiration 2029-08-03 (30 days).
- @Monica: coordinate with Legal/Finance to get the MOU scanned into the deal file and approve the nominal commitment; Finance to confirm billing flow if the customer converts and we need to transition to a billed Dedicated contract.
- @Ops (ops_capacity@redwood.ai): reserve the 12 GPUs, label nodes, and set scheduling affinity; deliver the runbook for warmup.
- @Michael: confirm with Samir that soft-hold until 2029-08-03 is acceptable and ask them to run the pre-warm within that window.

I’m OK to authorize the soft-sequestration pending Laura’s availability check; Laura — please post availability/impact by EOD and include the internal ticket number so we can track.

-Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
VP, Product Operations | Redwood Inference
